backlog.spec: Keep an exponential moving average of all trainable parameters, updated after each optimizer step with decay 0.995 once the first 50 percent of steps are done (copy the raw weights before that point). At the end of train(), copy the EMA values into the model's parameters so predict() uses them. Reset the EMA buffers at the start of each train() call, and do not touch them in predict(). Keep BatchNorm running stats as they are.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for the final model

backlog.spec: In predict(), apply the mirror-and-shift test-time augmentation to all test images instead of only the 25 percent least confident ones. Keep the same five views (original, top-left and bottom-right 2-pixel reflect crops, each with its flip) and average logits. This removes the uncertainty selection step and tests whether the extra accuracy is worth the added prediction time.
backlog.title: Flip and shift TTA on every test image

backlog.spec: Change UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE in the tta function from 0.25 to 0.5, so half of the test images receive the full set of augmented views. Nothing else changes. This is a one-number trade-off between prediction time and accuracy.
backlog.title: Larger uncertain fraction for TTA

backlog.spec: In the TTA path, replace the mean of logits over views with the mean of softmax probabilities, then take the log of the averaged probabilities as the returned logits so the output shape and argmax behaviour stay the same. Apply the same change to the mirror-only path if it is used. Keep everything else in predict() unchanged.
backlog.title: Average softmax probabilities in TTA

backlog.spec: Extend the TTA views in _get_tta_logits from three translations (center, top-left, bottom-right) to five by adding top-right and bottom-left 2-pixel reflect crops, all with their flips. Average the logits over all ten views for the uncertain images. Predicted cost increases only for the uncertain quarter of the test set.
backlog.title: Five-shift TTA views

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup, add a skip path that takes the block input, applies max-pool with kernel 2, and a 1x1 convolution (bias-free, channels_out outputs), and adds it to the output of norm2 before the final SiLU. Initialise the 1x1 projection weights to zero so the block starts identical to the current one. The rest of the network is unchanged.
backlog.title: Residual projection skip in each ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Replace nn.SiLU() in ConvGroup with nn.GELU() in both activation positions, keeping the rest of the network unchanged. The change is a single-line swap, but it affects the nonlinearity's shape near zero and may change accuracy at this short schedule.
backlog.title: GELU instead of SiLU in ConvGroup

backlog.spec: Before the linear head, compute both global average pooling and global max pooling over the final feature map (which is 1x1 after the last MaxPool, so use the channel vector twice), concatenate them, and feed the 512-dimensional result to the head. Adjust the head input size to match. Keep the head's 1/size scaling unchanged.
backlog.title: Concatenated average and max pooling before the head

backlog.spec: Change widths in CifarNet from block1=64, block2=256, block3=256 to block1=64, block2=192, block3=256. This reduces the cost of the largest convolution layer, and the epoch count can stay the same because the time-accuracy curve is handled by the script's existing trade-off.
backlog.title: Narrower middle block width

backlog.spec: Change whiten_kernel_size in CifarNet from 2 to 3. The whitening output then has 54 channels instead of 24, and init_whiten still builds the eigen-filters from patch covariance with the matching patch size, plus their negatives. Verify that the reshape in init_whiten still uses the right kernel shape. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Whitening kernel of size 3

backlog.spec: In the BatchNorm class, remove the line that sets self.weight.requires_grad to False so the scale parameter is learned. Keep the initial value of one. Update the optimizer parameter groups so the norm scales join the bias group (the code already selects parameters with 'norm' in the name, so they will be picked up automatically). The rest of training is unchanged.
backlog.title: Learned BatchNorm scale

backlog.spec: Give the linear head a bias term (bias=True) and initialise it to zero. Add it to the head parameter group that uses HEAD_LR and the same weight decay setting. Keep the 1/size output scaling on the whole head output, including the bias term, so only the bias dynamics change.
backlog.title: Trainable head bias

backlog.spec: In _zeropower_via_newtonschulz5, add one more copy of the Newton-Schulz update block (A = X X^T, B = b A + c A^2, X = a X + B X) so that the orthogonalisation uses four iterations instead of three. Keep the coefficients and the normalisation unchanged. This gives a more accurate orthogonalised update at a small extra cost.
backlog.title: Four Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: In the Muon step, multiply each filter's orthogonalised update by sqrt(max(1, rows/cols)) of its reshaped matrix (rows = output channels, cols = input channels times kernel area) before applying it with the learning rate. This gives tall filter matrices a larger step, as in common Muon variants. Compute the factor once per parameter at construction time and store it in filter_params_meta.
backlog.title: Aspect-ratio scaling of Muon updates

backlog.spec: Multiply the Muon learning rate by a linear warmup factor that rises from 0.1 to 1.0 over the first 3 percent of total training steps, then continues with the existing linear decay to zero. Apply the same warmup factor to the Nesterov SGD groups that use the same lr_factor2 schedule, or leave them unchanged if that is simpler. Implement it as an extra multiplier in the train loop where lr_factor2 is computed.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup for Muon learning rate

backlog.spec: Start MUON_MOMENTUM at 0.5 and ramp it linearly to its final value of 0.655 over the first 20 percent of training steps, then hold it constant. Update group['momentum'] for the Muon param group inside the train loop before each optimizer step. Keep the Nesterov form and all other Muon settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Momentum warmup for Muon

backlog.spec: Replace the linear decay multipliers lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 in the train loop with a cosine decay that goes from 1 at step 0 to 0 at total_train_steps, using 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress)). The whiten bias schedule can keep its linear shape. Apply it to both optimizers in the same way as the current linear factors.
backlog.title: Cosine decay instead of linear decay

backlog.spec: Keep all learning rate multipliers at 1.0 for the first 50 percent of total training steps, then decay them linearly to zero over the remaining steps. Apply this shape to the Muon and head/bias learning rates through the existing lr_factor2 path. This gives the optimizer more time at high learning rate before annealing.
backlog.title: Constant learning rate then linear decay

backlog.spec: Change WHITEN_BIAS_EPOCHS from 0.2 to 0.5, so the whitening bias keeps receiving gradients (and its learning rate decays) for a longer period. Nothing else changes. This tests whether the whitening bias benefits from more adaptation before it is frozen.
backlog.title: Longer whiten bias training

backlog.spec: Train with batch size 1024 for the first half of total steps and 2048 for the second half, both drawn from the same shuffled epoch. Build the loader so each epoch yields batches of the current size, and recompute steps_per_epoch so total_train_steps stays matched to the epoch count. Scale the weight decay term as the code already does (it multiplies by the batch size), and keep the learning rates unchanged. Mark the compiled forward step as dynamic=False so the two shapes each compile once.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp from 1024 to 2048

backlog.spec: Replace the epoch-level alternating flip with an independent random flip for each image in each epoch. Generate a boolean mask per sample with torch.rand and apply torch.where to the normalised images, as batch_flip_lr already does, but do it in every epoch rather than once per epoch. Keep the translation and colour jitter unchanged.
backlog.title: Per-sample random horizontal flip

backlog.spec: Change TRANSLATE from 2 to 3, so the reflect-padded images are 38 by 38 and random crops of 32 by 32 move by up to three pixels in each direction. The batch_crop function already computes its offsets from the padding size, so no other code changes are required. Keep the TTA padding at its current value.
backlog.title: Translation of 3 pixels

backlog.spec: For each training batch, pick half of the samples at random and zero an 8 by 8 square at a random location in the normalised image (zero is the dataset mean after normalisation). Implement it in a compiled helper with a mask built from arange comparisons against random centres, applied after translation and before colour jitter. Keep labels unchanged.
backlog.title: Cutout on half of each batch

backlog.spec: Set the color_jitter entry in the training augmentation dictionary to enabled False and remove the brightness and contrast perturbation. The flip and translation augmentations stay as they are. This is an ablation that checks whether the colour jitter helps at this training length or only costs time.
backlog.title: Remove colour jitter

backlog.spec: In train(), compute the whitening covariance from the first 5000 training images instead of the first 960, keeping the same patch extraction and eps. Compute the statistics on the normalised training images inside the run, with no reuse across runs. The whitening filters will be better estimated, at a small one-time cost in the timed run.
backlog.title: Whitening statistics from more images

backlog.spec: For the first 20 percent of training steps, downsample each batch from 32 by 32 to 24 by 24 with bilinear interpolation (antialias on), then use the full 32 by 32 inputs for the remaining steps. Make the training loop select the resize path by step, and keep the same batch size and labels. Because the whitening conv and pooling layers accept any size, the network needs no architectural change, but compile separate graphs for the two input sizes.
backlog.title: Low-resolution warm-up

backlog.spec: Start label smoothing at 0.0 and increase it linearly to LABEL_SMOOTHING (0.09) over the first 30 percent of training steps, then hold it. Pass the current value into the loss function through a tensor argument, or recompute the smoothed targets manually so the compiled forward step does not recompile on every change. Keep the loss reduction as sum.
backlog.title: Label smoothing ramp

backlog.spec: Change the compile mode of forward_step from max-autotune to reduce-overhead so the forward and backward pass runs under CUDA graphs, which removes kernel launch overhead for this small network. Keep fullgraph=True and make sure the inputs are copied into static buffers of fixed shape, which the fixed batch size already provides. Keep the optimizer steps as they are.
backlog.title: CUDA graphs for the forward and backward step

backlog.spec: Store the learning rates of the Nesterov SGD and Muon parameter groups as one-element CUDA tensors, and update them in place with a single fill or mul operation per step, instead of rebuilding Python floats in the loop. Use the tensor forms supported by the fused SGD and the Muon foreach updates, or convert them back to float where a tensor is not accepted. This removes host-side work and possible sync points in every training step.
backlog.title: Tensor-valued learning rates

backlog.spec: Change the head output scaling from dividing by x.size(-1) (the 256 feature width) to dividing by sqrt(x.size(-1)). Leave the head weight initialisation and its reset scaling (the 1/std normalisation in reset()) unchanged. This gives the logits a larger range at the start of training and changes the effective head learning rate, which may trade off against the tuned HEAD_LR.
backlog.title: Head scale of one over the square root of width

backlog.spec: Move model.head.weight out of the Nesterov SGD group and into the Muon optimizer, treating its 10x256 matrix as a 2D filter. Keep its learning rate at HEAD_LR scaled to the Muon scale, for example MUON_LR times 0.5, and keep the same linear decay to zero. Remove head_lr from the SGD param_configs. The head then receives Newton-Schulz orthogonalised updates, which may suit a short-horizon linear classifier better than raw SGD. The existing filter_params list only takes 4D tensors, so add the head to a separate Muon instance or extend the filter test to include 2D parameters named head.
backlog.title: Orthogonalised Muon update for the head

backlog.spec: Keep a single Muon optimizer but split the filter parameters into three param groups by block: conv weights of ConvGroup 1 use a multiplier of 0.6, ConvGroup 2 uses 1.0, and ConvGroup 3 uses 1.4 on top of MUON_LR. Each group keeps the same linear decay and the same weight decay. The Muon step currently reads group["lr"] from param_groups[0] only, so change the step to loop over groups, or run one Muon instance per block. The idea is that the early high-resolution filters and the late wide filters may want different step sizes under orthogonalised updates.
backlog.title: Layer-wise Muon learning-rate multipliers

backlog.spec: Replace the fused Nesterov SGD on the non-filter parameters (whiten bias, all BatchNorm biases) with torch.optim.AdamW using lr equal to BIAS_LR times 0.05 (about 0.003), betas (0.9, 0.99), eps 1e-8, and the same linear decay to zero. Keep weight decay at zero for these parameters. Leave the head on SGD. Keep the whiten bias freezing logic, which sets requires_grad through whiten_bias_grad, so the AdamW group still stops updating after whiten_bias_train_steps. This tests whether adaptive per-parameter scaling helps the few scalar biases that SGD currently handles.
backlog.title: AdamW for the scalar and bias parameters

backlog.spec: Extend the existing low-resolution warm-up into three stages instead of one. For the first 20 percent of total steps, interpolate inputs to 20x20 with antialiased bilinear. From 20 to 55 percent of steps, use 24x24. For the remaining steps use the full 32x32. Compute the stage boundaries from total_train_steps and keep the interpolation inside the training loop, as now. Because torch.compile is set with dynamic=False, each new input size will trigger one recompile, so warm up the forward_step at each size in the untimed first call if needed, or accept one extra recompile per size that is excluded from the timed runs only if it happens during the untimed call. Measure whether the extra stage helps.
backlog.title: Three-stage progressive resizing

backlog.spec: Set BATCH_SIZE to 768 and keep EPOCHS unchanged, so the number of optimizer steps doubles. Scale the learning rates to match: multiply MUON_LR and BIAS_LR and HEAD_LR by 1/sqrt(2), about 0.7, and set the weight decay per step as currently computed from training_batch_size. Adjust the low-resolution and whiten-bias step counts, which are already computed from len(train_loader), so they scale automatically. The loss is a sum with label smoothing, so the gradient scale per step changes with batch size; check that the head's 1/width scaling still gives a sensible step. This explores a different point on the step-count versus per-step cost curve.
backlog.title: Smaller batch with twice the steps

backlog.spec: Insert nn.Dropout2d(p=0.05) after norm2 and its SiLU in ConvGroup for block1 only, so it is applied to the 64-channel features. It is active only in train mode and is a no-op in predict, which already calls model.eval() inside infer. Keep the input to the compiled forward_step unchanged. The dropout must be created in __init__ and applied in forward, and it does not alter the whitening layer. The purpose is a mild regulariser on the early features, which the current augmentation-only setup may underfit or overfit only weakly at 7.65 epochs.
backlog.title: Channel dropout after the first block

backlog.spec: In each ConvGroup, after conv2 and norm2, add a 1x1 convolution with bias False that maps channels_out to channels_out, initialised as the identity with a small random perturbation, followed by a second BatchNorm without learned scale and then SiLU. Keep the existing 3x3 convolutions and max pool. Initialise the 1x1 weight through the same reset path so that model.reset() still works, or set it to the identity in reset_parameters. This is a bolder change that adds a pointwise nonlinear stage per block at modest cost, testing whether extra depth without extra spatial receptive field helps this short schedule.
backlog.title: Bottleneck 1x1 convolution in each block

backlog.spec: Replace each nn.MaxPool2d(2) in ConvGroup with a custom module that computes a learnable scalar alpha, initialised to 1.0, and returns alpha times max pooling plus (1 minus alpha) times average pooling, both with kernel 2 and stride 2. The scalar is a parameter with requires_grad True and no weight decay. Keep the module in half precision with the rest of the network so the model.half() loop still applies. Also replace the final nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with the same blend at global size. This lets the network choose between the two pooling types per stage, and it adds only a few parameters and almost no compute.
backlog.title: Learnable blend of max and average pooling

backlog.spec: Compute the loss per sample with reduction set to none in forward_step, detach it, and form weights proportional to the per-sample loss raised to the power 0.5, normalised so that the batch mean weight equals 1. Multiply the per-sample losses by these weights and sum them, keeping the sum reduction used now so that the Muon and SGD learning rates stay calibrated. Use the weights only after the first 30 percent of steps, and keep weight 1 before that. Because the weights are computed inside the compiled function from the batch's own losses, no data from earlier runs is reused. This emphasises hard examples in the later part of training.
backlog.title: Hard-example loss reweighting

backlog.spec: Change the linear decay for all optimizers so that the learning-rate factor decays from 1 to a floor of 0.1 instead of to 0. Concretely, replace lr_factor1 and lr_factor2 with max(0.1, 1 - step times the base factor) for the SGD and Muon groups, and keep the whiten bias group decaying to 0 as it does now. This keeps some optimisation signal at the end of training, which may help the final accuracy after the predict-time TTA, and it is a small change to the existing schedule code.
backlog.title: Non-zero floor on the final learning rate

backlog.spec: Change only predict(). For each test batch, run the model in train-mode BatchNorm so that normalisation uses the statistics of the test batch itself, while leaving the stored running_mean and running_var untouched (for example, save the buffers and restore them, or use F.batch_norm with training=True and running stats set to None inside a custom forward). Keep torch.no_grad(), keep the flip and shift TTA, and use batches of 2000 so the statistics are stable. predict() must still not change the model. Compare against the incumbent with the same training. This is a test-time-only change, so the training time is unchanged.
backlog.title: Transductive BatchNorm at prediction

backlog.spec: During training, for the last 35 percent of steps, apply CutMix to each batch with probability 0.5. Sample lambda from Beta(1,1), pick a random box covering about (1 - lambda) of the 32x32 area, paste the box from a randomly permuted copy of the batch, and set the targets to a mix of the two one-hot label vectors with the same lambda, using the label-smoothed targets. Keep the existing flip, shift and colour jitter. Do this inside the training loop before the compiled forward step, and keep the loss as the summed cross entropy with soft targets.
backlog.title: CutMix in the final third of training

backlog.spec: In ConvGroup for block 1 only, replace the nn.MaxPool2d(2) after conv1 with a 3x3 stride-2 convolution that has the same input and output widths, bias-free, with the same Dirac-style initialisation used by Conv. Keep the max pool in blocks 2 and 3. The order stays conv1, learned downsample, norm1, activation, conv2, norm2, activation. Because the pool is now a conv, the weight is a 4D tensor and is picked up by Muon automatically. Check that the stride-2 conv uses padding so the output is 16x16 when the input is 32x32 and 16x16 otherwise.
backlog.title: Learned strided downsampling in block 1

backlog.spec: Make the BatchNorm running-statistics momentum a function of training progress rather than a constant. Start the momentum at 0.5 at step 0 and decay it linearly to 0.1 at the final step, updating every BatchNorm module's momentum attribute before each forward step. This affects only the running statistics used by eval-mode inference, not the training forward pass. Keep the existing learning-rate schedules unchanged. Because the training-mode forward pass uses batch statistics, the effect should show up mainly in predict().
backlog.title: Annealed BatchNorm momentum

backlog.spec: Keep a float32 running average of all trainable parameters (the Muon filter weights, the norm biases, the whiten bias and the head) over the final 25 percent of optimizer steps, using a uniform average over those snapshots, so that after k snapshots the average is avg += (p - avg)/k. Take a snapshot after each optimizer step once the step count passes 75 percent of total_train_steps. Before predict(), copy the averaged parameters into the model in half precision, once per run inside train(). Do not use an exponential decay. Make sure the average is reinitialised at the start of each train() call and that the model is not left in an averaged state for the next run. This is different from the earlier EMA attempt because it is a uniform tail average with no decay constant.
backlog.title: Uniform tail averaging of iterates

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 2-pixel translation with a random scale-and-shift augmentation. For each batch, sample a scale s uniformly in [0.9, 1.0] and crop a window of side round(32*s) at a random offset from the reflect-padded image, then resize back to 32x32 with bilinear interpolation (antialias off). Use one scale per batch so that the operation can be applied with a single F.interpolate call on a sliced tensor. Keep the 2-pixel translate range inside the crop. Keep the flip, colour jitter and progressive resizing. The point is to add mild zoom diversity without changing the test-time pipeline.
backlog.title: Random-resized-crop scale jitter

backlog.spec: Increase the width of block 1 from 64 to 128 channels in the widths dictionary. Block 2 and block 3 keep 256 channels. The whitening output width of 24 is unchanged, and conv1 of block 1 maps 24 to 128 channels while conv2 maps 128 to 128 channels. The block-2 conv1 now takes 128 input channels. Check that all BatchNorm, pooling and the head width still match. This trades a moderate amount of extra compute in the first, highest-resolution block for capacity, so the time-accuracy balance may need the epoch count to be revisited within the same budget.
backlog.title: Wider first block

backlog.spec: Replace the Nesterov SGD optimizer for the whiten bias, the norm biases and the head with a Lion-style update. Keep an fp32 momentum buffer per parameter with beta1 = 0.9 for the update direction and beta2 = 0.99 for the buffer, then apply the update as p -= lr * sign(beta1 * m + (1 - beta1) * g), with weight decay applied as the decoupled term p *= (1 - lr * wd). Keep the existing per-group linear learning-rate decay to zero and the existing learning rates scaled by about 0.3 to start, since sign updates have unit magnitude. Muon stays unchanged for the convolution filters. The implementation should use torch._foreach ops or a single fused loop so the optimizer cost stays small.
backlog.title: Sign-based updates for scalar and bias parameters

backlog.spec: Order the training data by difficulty and let the easier examples come first in early epochs. After each epoch, record the per-example loss from the training forward pass in a float buffer indexed by the example index, updating it for the examples seen in that epoch. For the first epoch use a random order. For later epochs, draw each batch with probability proportional to a mix of uniform sampling and the previous loss, using 0.5 uniform and 0.5 loss-weighted sampling, which keeps the number of examples per epoch unchanged. Implement the sampling with torch.multinomial on a per-epoch weight vector computed once at the start of each epoch. The buffer must be allocated inside train() so that no state carries between runs.
backlog.title: Curriculum by previous-epoch loss

backlog.spec: Replace the final nn.AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with a flatten of the 4x4 map of block 3, so the head input is 256*4*4 = 4096 features instead of 256. Keep the head as a bias-free linear layer to 10 classes, but scale its input by one over the square root of the new fan-in as in the existing scaled head, and keep the head learning rate and weight decay rule unchanged. The block-3 output must be 4x4 when the input is 32x32 and 3x3 at the 24x24 stage, so either use AdaptiveAvgPool2d(4) before flattening to keep the head size fixed, or take the max over the spatial dimension for the low-resolution stages. The change adds a head with more parameters but almost no compute.
backlog.title: Spatial head instead of global max pool

incumbent.description: Replace the single low-resolution warm-up with three progressive-resizing stages: 20x20 for the first 20 percent of steps, 24x24 from 20 to 55 percent, and full 32x32 afterwards, with boundaries computed from total_train_steps.

memo: Helped: lower-resolution early training. Slot 0 (single low-res warm-up) scored -0.0683. Slot 9 (three-stage progressive resizing) was best at -0.1184 and -0.1212, so it is the incumbent (mean_adjusted -0.1136). Slot 15 (per-ConvGroup Muon lr groups) scored -0.1395 on one run, but it is unreplicated and rejected against the incumbent. Slot 4 (Muon momentum ramp) scored -0.0973 and -0.1026, so it is slightly worse than the incumbent. Did not help: colour jitter off (-0.0563), TTA change (-0.0529), label smoothing ramp (-0.0755), translate 3 (-0.0570), learnable BatchNorm scale (+0.0714), skip projection (1.1254), head in Muon (3.8105), Lion-style optimizer (0.1510). Optimizer and architecture changes mostly failed (a=1, b=5 each). Crashes: OOM in TTA and non-finite half-precision logits. Slot 16 (EMA) was invalid (first_run_differs). Next: tune stage sizes and boundaries on the slot 9 base, and combine with the slot 15 or slot 4 ideas. Replicate any gain, since differences under about 0.03 are noise.
